verification.notes: Official FBI statements confirm that a rifle was recovered in a wooded area along the escape path. Current official and court sources reviewed do not corroborate the specific sequence that explosives-detection dogs first searched the location unsuccessfully and that federal agents then directed two rookie officers to repeat the search. The recovery is supported; the dog and direction sequence remains unverified.

appearances.snippet: I've been given two names I've had these names for a long time ... and one of them had only just graduated from UVU I'm not kidding talk about beginner's luck I'm told Mitchell Curtiss of Pleasant Grove Police ... 2025 graduate very young buck he finds this gun

verification.notes: The claim is attributed to anonymous government sources. Current searches found no official roster, sworn testimony, police release, graduation record, or reliable named-source report that independently confirms Mitchell Curtiss was the finding officer and a 2025 Utah Valley University graduate. The private-source claim remains attempted/unverifiable.

records.text: Owens said Foster Curtiss is Mitchell Curtiss's father and served 21 years with NCIS, ending as a division chief in the Office of Inspector General.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: His father's name is Foster Curtiss. ... Foster (Foster Curtiss) spent 21 years. ... With NCIS starting as a special agent and working his way up the ladder, ending up as the division chief in the Office of Inspector General.

verification.notes: Public records support that Foster Curtiss served as an NCIS special agent/division chief in its Office of Inspector General and later joined Richmond's inspector-general office. The reviewed public sources do not independently establish the father-son relationship to Mitchell Curtiss or the exact 21-year tenure. Career-role details are supported, while the relationship and duration remain uncorroborated.
